ID-senate.statusNote: Sen. Jim Risch (R) won the May 19 primary with about 67% and seeks a fourth term. Democratic nominee David Roth withdrew July 28, leaving independent former state Rep. Todd Achilles as Risch's main challenger.

ID-governor.statusNote: Gov. Brad Little (R) won the May 19 primary with about 59%, defeating seven GOP challengers, and seeks a third term against Boise attorney Terri Pickens (D), who won her primary with about 61%. Also on the November ballot: independent former Idaho Supreme Court Justice John Stegner, Libertarian Paul Sand and Constitution Party candidate Pro-Life.

ID-house-1.statusNote: Rep. Russ Fulcher (R) seeks re-election against Kaylee Peterson (D), Constitution Party candidate Brendan Gomez and independent Sarah Zabel. Fulcher won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with about 78% and Peterson won the Democratic primary with about 87%. Positions researched and stored, race not scored, overlap 0 of 10 as of Aug 29, 2026.

candidates.name: Jim Risch

climate.label: Touts that the reconciliation bill 'ends the Green New Deal, also known as the Green New Scam' (Senate office)

education.label: Strongly favors vouchers for school choice (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: Favors stricter punishment as a crime deterrent (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Strongly opposes abortion as a woman's unrestricted right (Ballotpedia)

candidates.name: Todd Achilles
candidates.now: Independent U.S. Senate candidate; former Idaho state representative

Became Risch's main challenger after Democratic nominee David Roth withdrew July 28; he had outraised Roth roughly $692,000 to $8,600.
priorities: Lower costs through price transparency and anti-price-fixing rules
Term limits and ending congressional stock trading

health.label: Protect health care tax credits and pursue cross-party insurance reforms plus price transparency (campaign policies)

immigration.label: Mixed: backs Customs and Border Protection staffing, technology, and resources 'to secure our border' AND a modernized visa system with revived bipartisan immigration reform (campaign policies)

taxes.label: 'Lower taxes for working families, small businesses, and ag producers' while closing corporate tax loopholes (campaign policies)

education.label: Calls strong public schools essential to Idaho's future; supports federal education funding and investment in career and technical education and apprenticeships (campaign policies)

repro.label: Supports Idaho's Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act ballot initiative and says voters should decide (campaign policies)

candidates.name: Brad Little
candidates.background: Governor since 2019 and lieutenant governor before that; ran his family's ranching operation for nearly 30 years. Won the May 19 Republican primary with about 59% over Mark Fitzpatrick (29%) and six others, and is seeking a third term on a record of 'lower taxes, reign in government, invest in what matters most.'
priorities: Record tax relief
Managing growth: schools, roads, water and housing
Immigration enforcement

cost.label: Frames affordability through 'record tax relief': the 2025 session delivered over $400M in cuts including a $155 per year grocery tax credit (Idaho Capital Sun)

health.label: Signed HB 345 seeking Medicaid work requirements: 'reasonably reeling in Medicaid spending so taxpayers are not overly burdened' (Idaho Capital Sun via Yahoo)

housing.label: Proposed putting $50 million of federal relief funds into gap financing for workforce housing, projected to build about 1,000 units (BoiseDev)

immigration.label: Signed HB 83 creating state crimes of illegal entry and illegal reentry plus penalties for transporting unauthorized immigrants with prior convictions; a federal court blocked it the same day after the ACLU sued (Idaho Capital Sun)

taxes.label: Praised the session's 'record tax relief', including HB 40 dropping individual and corporate income tax rates from 5.695% to 5.3%, part of over $400M in 2025 cuts (Idaho Capital Sun)

education.label: Mixed: signed HB 93 directing $50M to private school tuition tax credits, saying Idaho can 'have it all, strong public schools and education freedom', while conceding 'there's not enough accountability in it' (Idaho Capital Sun)

safety.label: Signed HB 380 allowing the death penalty for child sexual abuse: 'the perpetrators deserve the ultimate punishment' (Idaho Capital Sun)

repro.label: Signed the six-week abortion bans HB 366 (2021) and SB 1309 (2022) and the 2023 'abortion trafficking' law criminalizing helping minors travel for abortions (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Signed HB 124 (2023) removing student IDs from acceptable voter identification (Democracy Docket)

candidates.name: Russell Fulcher
candidates.background: U.S. Representative since 2019, previously an Idaho state senator and 2014 gubernatorial candidate; small-business owner in real estate and insurance. Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with about 78%.
priorities: Cut federal taxes and regulatory burden
Shift natural-resource management from federal to state control
Limit the federal role in education and healthcare

cost.label: Pledges to 'cut taxes the way I got a grocery tax credit, returning more than $600 million per year to Idaho's hardworking families' and to reduce 'federal tax and regulatory burdens' (Ballotpedia)

health.label: Opposes eliminating the ACA outright, calling it a 'landmine' issue, and instead backs a 'voluntary parallel path' letting people choose private marketplace insurance directly (Idaho Capital Sun); also favors tax-free Health Savings Accounts and opposes Medicaid expansion in favor of 'personal responsibility' (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: Voted yes on the Laken Riley Act, S.5, Jan 22, 2025 (House roll call 23)

taxes.label: Voted yes on H.R. 1, the 2025 reconciliation tax law, Jul 3, 2025 (House roll call 190)

climate.label: Backs the Lower Energy Costs Act and moving to 'unleash responsibly our natural resources to create business and job opportunities,' shifting management 'from the federal government to the people [and] State of Idaho' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Believes 'the federal government should limit its role in education' and backs 'public, private, charter, digital or home school' options with 'the success of the student' as the goal (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Voted yes on the SAVE Act, H.R. 22, Apr 10, 2025 (House roll call 102)

nullNotes.housing: checked Ballotpedia and Idaho Capital Sun healthcare-costs roundup, nothing documented (checked 2026-08-29)
nullNotes.safety: checked Ballotpedia; voted for the Secure the Border Act of 2023 (scored under immigration) and opposes prolonged military engagement, no domestic policing/sentencing position documented (checked 2026-08-29)
nullNotes.repro: checked Ballotpedia; page lists 'Supporting Life' as a campaign theme with no elaborated position, and a 2014 Idaho Chooses Life endorsement is not his own statement, so left null (checked 2026-08-29)

candidates.name: Kaylee Jade Peterson
candidates.background: Idaho Democrat making her third run for the 1st District seat, campaigning on affordability, single-payer healthcare, and public education funding. Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with about 87%.
priorities: Single-payer, Medicare-for-all style healthcare
Break up monopolies driving up housing and grocery prices
Fully federally fund public education, pre-K through higher ed

cost.label: Would 'break up monopolies' that 'artificially inflate prices,' citing large investment firms owning 26% of single-family homes (campaign issues page)

health.label: 'The government needs to step in... we're not also paying the taxes for healthcare and paying thousands of dollars a month,' backing 'a universal single-payer system' (Idaho Capital Sun); campaign site calls taking insurers 'completely out of the equation... the cheapest way forward'

housing.label: Opposes corporate ownership of single-family homes and backs revising the tax code to favor local builders (campaign issues page)

immigration.label: Criticizes 'warrantless arrests, unconstitutional home searches' and 'keeping children in dangerous, unsafe facilities' in enforcement, while backing streamlined legal pathways (campaign issues page)

taxes.label: Would 'increase corporate tax rates, remove corporate tax breaks/subsidies' while offering middle-class relief (campaign issues page)

climate.label: Backs renewable energy 'to lower utility bills' and opposes fossil fuel subsidies (campaign issues page)

education.label: Supports 'fully federally funding public education from pre-K through higher education' and opposes diverting 'a single cent of taxpayer funds' to private education (campaign issues page)

repro.label: Notes Idaho has 'lost 43% of our practicing OBGYNs' since Dobbs and says lawmakers should 'step out of the exam room and listen to women' (campaign issues page)
